The thing is, we don't want moderators just because they live in a specific time zones. They have to be a quality moderator, and one that can represent Avicus in a good light. replies.author: MasterProX
replies.body:
If that is so, then you clearly do not understand — how can the staff be "not interested in this problem" when, on any given day, around one dozen requests are made on Slack for other moderators to come online? Moderators are promoted because they meet or exceed performance expectations, not purely to fill a vacant time zone slot. This is comparable to the way reputable companies (generally) do not hire applicants to balance the numbers of males and females, or to equally represent every ethnicity; they simply select the ones with the most experience, or the ones they believe will work the hardest. For us, and for many, it is the most efficient and promising method.

Staff applications are — as far as I'm aware — never denied because of the player's time zone, but rather because the player applying is not up to standards as a whole, and for that same reason we do not particularly view their time zone as a deciding factor. Furthermore, we already do occasionally "ask the players that are often online" if they would like to be promoted, but, again, this only occurs if they are projected to be "good enough" to benefit the staff team with minimal risk.

People in this community already voice many complaints about various staff members, typically those who were deemed satisfactory to earn their promotion(s). If the current moderators who went through formal processes to reach their positions appear questionable in the community's eyes, I can only imagine what everyone will think about untrained lunatics dishing out false bans during the hours that no one else is online to issue correct punishments instead.

replies.author: PokerFace
replies.body:
More staff will only be inactive while they are online. It's not like since there are 60ish staff that people would go on leave more often, it's just that each individual would take less reports due to the higher amount of staff. That way, it is more distributed among the moderators.  

The moderators became moderators to moderate regularly, not to be inactive.

I may not be active anymore but I've been here for 2 years.

I know what it's like as a player when no staff are on and hackers are everywhere.

I also know as a staff member, being the only moderator online, having to answer 3 reports all at the same time.

I've experienced more than you have and have experienced a lot of diverse situations in my 2 years so don't make assumptions mate.

replies.author: Murphh
replies.body:
While playing nebula, I've noticed the lack of mods online at certain hours as well and it can be frustrating.  Some players are suggesting that we should just record and report.  Well, I don't log onto avicus to "play mod".  I don't automatically have my recording software ready to go or just go ahead and record every game I play just in case someone hacks.  That makes no sense.  It feels like you're blaming the victim when you say, "You should have recorded..."

If the managers of avicus think that they have enough staff, then there should be some sort of organized staffing.  If this is a 24 hour server, than all the hours of the day should be covered by at least one mod.  Some players even suggested using skype, ts, or text to notify a mod to come online.  The majority of players don't have this information.  This is unrealistic.

In addition to hackers, there has been an increase in "troll" or "griefing" behavior while defending the monument. Players spamming blocks randomly in front of the mon, removing slabs & trapdoors, spleefing players into void, etc...  This is annoying as well with no mods online to take reports.  Or in some cases, a mod is online, but they are too busy, in a scrim or trying to get the mon, to respond promptly.

Wouldn't it make sense, if you have over 24 mods, that each mod could be online for 1 hour a day?  If you have to fill certain time periods then you find qualified players, that are awake and available, to be mod for those times. 

List of Mod qualities:
#1 Reliable and "on time"
# 2 Friendly
#3 Able to ID hacks
#4 Accessible
